doc.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Structure in music and projects from hell
summary: He says no structure is as complex as total structure and good music is good music, and describes a gig ruined by a duo partner's disrespect for the music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: What’s the — of the recordings you’ve done does one stand out as being let’s say the least structured and was it a challenge?
No I can’t come up with any. No. Because no structure is just as structured as the most complex structured, to me.

Okay. I’ll say it again. Having no structure is just as complex as having the greatest amount of structure or the greatest detailed structure. So in other words if somebody writes a chart that is totally through composed, everything has to be read, there’s no improvisation, in other words you’re in jail interpreting this chart, and on the other hand if you have absolutely nothing to go on, let’s just say somebody says we’re going to now do “Avarice,” that’s our theme, now you guys come up with avarice, that’s just as complex as going through this totally written out chart. That’s my point. Which brings me to the real principle which is good music is good music, lousy music is lousy music, just like Duke Ellington said. To me that’s it. So I can’t think — I mean most of the projects that I’ve been involved in I haven’t really had too many projects from hell. Somebody asked me last night at dinner, “Tell me about one or two of your projects” — not projects but was it recordings, no gigs — “from hell.” And I had to think about it. I could think of some where the working conditions or the living conditions or something were a drag, but generally speaking I can’t really think. I can think of a couple of times when the music was really a drag. But I wouldn’t call that from hell. It just was a drag because I took this gig and I’m working with this guy, maybe a duo, and he turns out to be a real asshole, a real jerk, and up to that point he’d been a friend and we’d even played some and whatnot. But he got so into something else that it spilled into the music and the

music was being just kind of shunted out by whatever obsession was stuck there. And I got angry because of that, not because of either pissed off at him in friendship or lack of friendship or anything, but just because he was being so disrespectful to the music.
